# BINDING CONSISTENCY LEDGER — Latvian Listening Pod (15 Scenes)

## 1. TRANSLITERATION
Not needed — names stay as written. Latvian uses Latin script with diacritics (ā, ē, ī, ū, š, ž, č, ģ, ķ, ļ, ņ). All personal names (Sarah, James, Anna, Davies, Jones) and place names (Manchester, London, France) remain unchanged in Latvian dialogue.

## 2. PRICES
- £8.40 → astoņi eiro četrdesmit centi (or colloquially astoņi četrdesmit)
- £12.50 → divpadsmit eiro piecdesmit centi (or divpadsmit piecdesmit)

## 3. TARGET-LANGUAGE NAME
When referring to the language: **latviešu valoda** (formal) or **latvieši** (colloquial "Latvian" as a noun). In everyday speech by learners: "I'm learning **latvieši**" or "I'm learning **latviešu**."

## 4. RECURRING LINES

| Canonical | Latvian Rendering |
|-----------|-------------------|
| Good morning | Labrīt |
| Good afternoon | Labdien |
| Good evening | Labvakar |
| How are you? | Kā jums klājas? (formal) / Kā tev klājas? (informal) |
| See you later / See you then | Uz redzēšanos |
| What can I get you? | Ko es varu jums nozīmēt? (formal) / Ko es varu tev nozīmēt? (informal) |
| I'd like… please | Es gribētu…, lūdzu |
| Thank you / Thank you very much | Paldies / Paldies daudz |
| Goodbye | Uz redzēšanos / Viss labais |
| Pleased to meet you | Prieks iepazīties |
| I'm learning Latvian | Es mācos latviešu (valodu) |
| Could you say that again more slowly? | Vai jūs varētu to atkārtot lēnāk? |
| Would you like to sit-in or takeaway? | Jūs vēlētos iekšā vai līdzi? |
| Could I pay by card? | Vai es varētu maksāt ar karti? |
| Do you have…? | Vai jums ir…? |
| Excuse me | Atvainojiet (formal) / Atvainojies (informal) |
| Yes, of course | Jā, protams |
| Thank you, you've been very helpful | Paldies, jūs bijāt ļoti noderīgi |
| You're welcome | Lūdzu / Nav par ko |

## 5. REGISTER

- **Customer–Staff / Strangers:** Use **jūs** (formal you). Polite, moderate tone. One *lūdzu* per request. Staff addressing customer in formal settings (restaurant, hotel, shop): **jūs**. Younger baristas in casual cafés may use **tu** with younger customers — both acceptable.
- **Peer / Friends:** Use **tu** (informal you). Casual contracted forms natural (es gribētu → es gribēju). Moderate politeness; Latvians do not over-mark courtesy.
- **Neighbour (morning/evening):** Use **jūs** (respectful but neighbourly). Not stiff.
